text:
mika: Heads up — I just exported a saved search CSV (Ad-hoc export) and the file contains a hidden/internal column called `org_id`. Not good.

olivia: ugh, do you have a sample of the header/rows? can you paste first 5 lines? :eyes: @mika

mika: pasted first lines:
```
id,name,email,org_id
123,Jane Doe,jane@example.com,org_prod_42
456,Acme Inc,dev+acme@example.com,org_acme_7
```

sam: oh that looks like the DB projection slipped straight through the exporter. We should never expose internal tenant ids in CSV.

raj: questions: 1) is this just saved-search exports from console UI or also API exports? 2) any PII columns leaking too or just org_id?

mika: reproduced via console UI > Saved Searches > Export rows. Not via public API yet (haven't tried). The CSV contains only org_id as the extra column — no SSNs or emails masked, just already present columns plus org_id.

olivia: thanks. likely cause: the export code reuses the DB select clause (select *) and then UI maps columns by column names. Quick mitigation: hide org_id column in front-end if present, but we need server-side sanitization.

raj: agree. Frontend bandaid is OK for immediate customer-facing but not sufficient. Plan: sanitize export projection on the export service to whitelist columns per saved-search schema.

sam: +1. Also add a unit test that exports a row with a fake internal column and assert it's stripped.

qa_bot: QA checklist created: EXPORT-PRIV-5612. Steps: reproduce, verify sanitized output, validate telemetry event. Assigned to qa-team.

mika: I opened an internal issue: ENG-5612 "Export service: strip internal tenant columns (org_id) from CSV" and attached sample CSV. Assigned to @raj.

raj: preliminary patch: change exporter to accept an explicit column list from the saved-search model (we already store visible_columns). If missing, default to read-only whitelist based on column metadata (visible==true). Also explicitly drop columns matching /(^|_)org(_|$)/i and internal_meta.*

olivia: strong 👍 on using visible_columns. Also: we should add a pre-commit lint rule on query projections for console-backed saved searches so new saved searches can't reference internal columns by mistake.

sam: rollout plan: patch -> deploy to staging -> canary 10% of console users -> monitor telemetry: export_count, export_failures, export_privacy_violations -> then 100% in 24h if no regressions.

raj: I'll scope the PR: code change in export-service + migration to backfill any saved-searches that have visible_columns=null by setting visible_columns from current UI mapping. Estimated 1 day dev + 1 day qa.

mika: FYI, customer reported via support (ticket #C-9871). We should notify them once fix is deployed and include sanitized CSV for them.

olivia: add a tiny console banner/notice for affected orgs? maybe not necessary if fixed quickly. We'll coordinate with support.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: export-service v3.2.1 -> staging at 1729457000 by raj

raj: staging deploy passed smoke tests. QA to validate EXPORT-PRIV-5612 now.

qa_bot: QA: validated staging exports. org_id absent from CSVs on staging. Marking test as PASS.

raj: rolling out canary to 10% at 1729457200. Adding temporary log metric export.privacy_strip=true for first 1000 exports.

sam: adding observability tickets: instrumentation for number of columns stripped, and counter when a saved-search references internal columns. Will add dashboard tile under Console->Privacy.

mika: thanks all. Please post PR link when ready. After canary, I'll coordinate support response.

raj: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/export-service/pull/289 — includes unit tests, migration, and blacklist config. Requesting review from @olivia @sam.

olivia: reviewing now. left 2 comments about column metadata edge cases.

sam: lgtm after comments. We should also add a short e2e test that runs on the staging pipeline to verify exported headers.

mika: support notified. I'll draft customer response once canary looks clean. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
